plan: In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of competitors' bids or strategies. This is because you pay the second-highest bid if you win, not your own bid, so there's no incentive to shade your bid. Since my value is $49 (the maximum possible), bidding my true value maximizes my expected profit and ensures I capture the full surplus when I win, since I only pay what the second-highest bidder bid.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction, where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of others' bids. My value is $1, which is very low. Bidding above my value risks losing money if I win at a price above $1; bidding below risks losing a profitable opportunity. Since I pay the second-highest bid if I win, truthful bidding maximizes expected profit. I'll bid exactly $1.

In a second-price auction, bidding one's true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of bidders or their behavior. This is because the payment depends on the second-highest bid, not my own bid, so bidding higher than my value risks overpaying, while bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. With a value of $16, I should bid exactly $16 to maximize expected profit.
